-- Migration 261: Admin Platform — Plans table
-- Stores subscription plan definitions for the ISAFlow Admin Platform.
-- Plans control feature access and billing amounts per company.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plans (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  code VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT,
  monthly_price_cents INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  annual_price_cents INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  currency VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  features JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  limits JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  display_order INT DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Starter: R299/mo, R2990/yr — 1 user, core accounting + invoicing
INSERT INTO plans (code, name, description, monthly_price_cents, annual_price_cents, currency, limits, display_order)
VALUES (
  'starter',
  'Starter',
  'Core accounting and invoicing for sole traders and micro businesses.',
  29900,
  299000,
  'ZAR',
  '{"max_users": 1, "max_companies": 1}',
  1
)
ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING;

-- Professional: R599/mo, R5990/yr — 5 users, + payroll, multi-company, bank feeds, document capture
INSERT INTO plans (code, name, description, monthly_price_cents, annual_price_cents, currency, limits, display_order)
VALUES (
  'professional',
  'Professional',
  'Full-featured accounting with payroll, bank feeds, and document capture for growing businesses.',
  59900,
  599000,
  'ZAR',
  '{"max_users": 5, "max_companies": 3}',
  2
)
ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING;

-- Enterprise: R1499/mo, R14990/yr — unlimited users, + API, custom reports, priority support
INSERT INTO plans (code, name, description, monthly_price_cents, annual_price_cents, currency, limits, display_order)
VALUES (
  'enterprise',
  'Enterprise',
  'Unlimited users, API access, custom reports, group consolidation, and priority support.',
  149900,
  1499000,
  'ZAR',
  '{"max_users": null, "max_companies": null}',
  3
)
ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING;

-- Migration 262: Admin Platform — Subscriptions and admin invoices
-- subscriptions tracks each company's active plan and billing cycle.
-- admin_invoices is intentionally prefixed to avoid conflict with the
-- accounting-module invoices table.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS subscriptions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  plan_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES plans(id),
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('trial', 'active', 'past_due', 'cancelled', 'paused')),
  billing_cycle VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT 'monthly' CHECK (billing_cycle IN ('monthly', 'annual')),
  current_period_start TIMESTAMPTZ,
  current_period_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
  cancel_at_period_end BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  cancelled_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  stripe_subscription_id VARCHAR(255),
  discount_percent INT DEFAULT 0,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_subscriptions_company ON subscriptions(company_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_subscriptions_status ON subscriptions(status);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS admin_invoices (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
  subscription_id UUID REFERENCES subscriptions(id),
  invoice_number VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'sent', 'paid', 'overdue', 'cancelled', 'credited')),
  subtotal_cents INT NOT NULL,
  tax_cents INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_cents INT NOT NULL,
  currency VARCHAR(3) DEFAULT 'ZAR',
  due_date DATE,
  paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  payment_method VARCHAR(50),
  stripe_invoice_id VARCHAR(255),
  line_items JSONB DEFAULT '[]',
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_admin_invoices_company ON admin_invoices(company_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_admin_invoices_status ON admin_invoices(status);

tool_input.prompt:
Create Phase 2 billing API routes for ISAFlow Admin Platform. All routes are super_admin only.

## Pattern

Look at existing admin API routes at `pages/api/admin/companies.ts` or `pages/api/admin/dashboard-stats.ts` for the exact pattern:
- `import { withAuth, withRole, type AuthenticatedNextApiRequest } from '@/lib/auth';`
- `import { withErrorHandler } from '@/lib/api-error-handler';`
- `import { apiResponse } from '@/lib/apiResponse';`
- Export: `export default withAuth(withRole('super_admin')(withErrorHandler(handler as any) as any) as any);`
- Method checking with `if (req.method === 'GET')`
- Always end with `apiResponse.methodNotAllowed()`
- Audit logging for mutations via `logAdminAction` from `@/modules/admin/services/auditService`

## Services to Import

From `@/modules/admin/services/planService`:
- `listPlans(includeArchived?)`, `getPlan(id)`, `createPlan(data)`, `updatePlan(id, data)`, `archivePlan(id)`

From `@/modules/admin/services/billingService`:
- `getBillingOverview()`, `listSubscriptions(filters)`, `getSubscription(id)`, `createSubscription(data)`, `updateSubscription(id, data)`, `cancelSubscription(id, atPeriodEnd)`, `listInvoices(filters)`, `createInvoice(data)`, `markInvoicePaid(id, method)`, `sendInvoice(id)`

From `@/modules/admin/services/auditService`:
- `logAdminAction(adminUserId, action, targetType, targetId, details, ipAddress)`

## Routes to Create

### `pages/api/admin/billing/overview.ts`
- GET: call `getBillingOverview()`, return result

### `pages/api/admin/billing/plans.ts`
- GET: `listPlans(req.query.include_archived === 'true')`
- POST: parse body `{ code, name, description, monthly_price_cents, annual_price_cents, currency, features, limits, display_order }`, call `createPlan(body)`, log audit `plan.create`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/plans/[id].ts`
- GET: `getPlan(id)`, 404 if not found
- PATCH: parse body, call `updatePlan(id, body)`, log audit `plan.update`
- DELETE: call `archivePlan(id)`, log audit `plan.archive`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/subscriptions.ts`
- GET: parse query filters `{ status, plan_id, search, page, limit }`, call `listSubscriptions(filters)`
- POST: parse body `{ company_id, plan_id, billing_cycle, discount_percent, notes }`, call `createSubscription(body)`, log audit `subscription.create`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/subscriptions/[id].ts`
- GET: `getSubscription(id)`, 404 if not found
- PATCH: parse body, call `updateSubscription(id, body)`, log audit `subscription.update`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/subscriptions/[id]/cancel.ts`
- POST: parse `{ at_period_end }` from body (boolean), call `cancelSubscription(id, at_period_end)`, log audit `subscription.cancel`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/invoices.ts`
- GET: parse query filters `{ company_id, status, from_date, to_date, search, page, limit }`, call `listInvoices(filters)`
- POST: parse body `{ company_id, subscription_id, subtotal_cents, tax_cents, total_cents, due_date, line_items, notes }`, call `createInvoice(body)`, log audit `invoice.create`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/invoices/[id]/send.ts`
- POST: call `sendInvoice(id)`, log audit `invoice.send`

### `pages/api/admin/billing/invoices/[id]/mark-paid.ts`
- POST: parse `{ payment_method }`, call `markInvoicePaid(id, payment_method)`, log audit `invoice.mark_paid`

## Audit Pattern
```typescript
const ip = (req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] as string)?.split(',')[0] || req.socket?.remoteAddress || null;
await logAdminAction(req.user.id, 'plan.create', 'plan', planId, { ...data }, ip);
```

Create all necessary directories. Follow exact existing patterns.

payload.prompt:
View the following comments from my business partner who's a 45 year veteran accountant and give me your opinion. Compare what he said to the features we've got, the functionality we've got and check what we can do to improve.

Key Challenges and Practical Improvements for Accounting Software Usability
Accounting software users worldwide face several recurring issues that impact efficiency, accuracy, and overall satisfaction. Organising these challenges and suggested improvements in logical order can help clarify both the problems and the solutions:
1. Usability and Complexity
•    Poor usability and unintuitive interfaces lead to steep learning curves and slow workflows.
•    Complex navigation and lack of intuitive design reduce productivity and increase user frustration.
2. System Integration and Data Entry
•    Limited integration with banking, payroll, CRM, and inventory systems causes duplicated work and inconsistent data.
•    Excessive manual data entry increases the risk of errors and inefficiencies.
3. Data Accuracy and Error Risks
•    Minor input errors can cascade through the system, resulting in incorrect reports and flawed reconciliations.
•    Maintaining data accuracy is critical for reliable financial decision-making.
4. Performance and Reliability
•    System lag, slow processing, crashes, and bugs are common in both cloud-based and desktop software.
5. Reporting and Compliance
•    Reporting tools are often inflexible, difficult to customise, or lack real-time insights.
•    Compliance challenges arise when software is not regularly updated or configured for tax, VAT/GST, or accounting standards.
6. Customer Support and Cost
•    Inadequate customer support is a frequent complaint, particularly for small and medium businesses.
•    Cost concerns include subscription fatigue with cloud solutions and high upfront/maintenance costs with desktop software.
7. Migration and Vendor Lock-in
•    Migrating to new systems is complex due to data transfer issues, limited export functionality, and vendor lock-in.
8. Cloud vs. Desktop Solutions
•    Cloud systems: Offer accessibility and easy integration but depend on internet connectivity, involve ongoing costs, and may have limited advanced features or privacy concerns.
•    Desktop systems: Provide greater control and customisation, but limit remote access and collaboration, and require manual backups and complex maintenance.
9. Industry and Business Size Preferences
•    SMEs often choose cloud solutions for lower upfront costs and flexibility but may outgrow them as needs become complex.
•    Large enterprises prefer desktop or hybrid ERP systems for advanced processes and control, accepting higher costs and longer implementations.
•    Industry needs vary: Professional services, retail, and e-commerce lean toward cloud; manufacturing, construction, and logistics require robust on-premises or hybrid systems; regulated industries prioritise compliance and data governance.

Practical System Improvements Highlighted by Users
•    Bank allocation: Streamline processes and improve transaction referencing, especially with multiple accounts.
•    Search functionality: Enable searching by both account name and number.
•    Navigation: Simplify navigation within financial categories; introduce shortcuts and direct access to account ranges.
•    VAT and audit support: Enhance VAT reporting, audit trails, and support detailed regulatory requirements.
•    Transaction controls: Allow configurable thresholds for high-value transactions to strengthen governance.
•    Interface design: Use intuitive, button-driven layouts over traditional menus.
•    Account mapping: Facilitate integration with financial statement software.
•    User access controls: Provide granular, role-based restrictions.
•    Period selection: Allow flexible access to company data by period.
•    Reporting: Offer adaptable, comprehensive reporting, including standard cash flow statements and IFRS-compliant financials.
•    Excel exports: Export data in analysis-ready formats, avoiding merged cells; present transactions with all relevant details.
•    Debit/credit display: Let users choose between separate columns or net values.

The Role of Content Optimisation
Content optimisation addresses many of these challenges by ensuring that financial data and documentation are well-organised, consistent, and free from duplication. Key aspects include:
•    Clean, consistent data across all records.
•    Optimised data storage for system performance.
•    Accurate and meaningful reporting.
•    Standardised transaction descriptions and account naming for better audits, compliance, and communication.
•    Elimination of redundant data and archiving of historical records to maintain performance.
In summary, content optimisation in accounting systems is foundational to supporting data accuracy, operational efficiency, and informed decision-making by ensuring all financial information is well-structured, reliable, and easily usable.

-- Approval Workflows
-- Configurable approval rules for invoices, payments, journal entries, credit notes

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approval_rules (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  document_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'customer_invoice', 'supplier_invoice', 'payment', 'journal_entry', 'credit_note'
  condition_field TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'total', -- 'total', 'amount'
  condition_operator TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'greater_than', -- 'greater_than', 'greater_equal', 'any'
  condition_value NUMERIC(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
  approver_role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin', -- 'admin', 'manager', 'accountant'
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  priority INTEGER DEFAULT 100,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approval_requests (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  rule_id UUID REFERENCES approval_rules(id),
  document_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  document_id UUID NOT NULL,
  document_reference TEXT, -- INV-001, JE-042, etc.
  amount NUMERIC(15,2),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', -- pending, approved, rejected, cancelled
  requested_by UUID NOT NULL,
  requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  decided_by UUID,
  decided_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  decision_notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Seed some default rules
INSERT INTO approval_rules (name, document_type, condition_field, condition_operator, condition_value, approver_role) VALUES
('Large customer invoices', 'customer_invoice', 'total', 'greater_than', 50000, 'manager'),
('Large supplier invoices', 'supplier_invoice', 'total', 'greater_than', 50000, 'manager'),
('Large payments', 'payment', 'amount', 'greater_than', 100000, 'admin'),
('All journal entries', 'journal_entry', 'total', 'any', 0, 'accountant'),
('Credit notes over R10k', 'credit_note', 'total', 'greater_than', 10000, 'manager')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_approval_requests_status ON approval_requests(status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_approval_requests_document ON approval_requests(document_type, document_id);

/**
 * Migration 210: VAT201 Data Model Enhancement
 *
 * Adds vat_type classification to journal lines and supplier invoice items
 * to support proper SARS VAT201 return reporting.
 *
 * SA VAT types:
 *   standard       — 15% standard rate supplies/purchases
 *   zero_rated     — 0% zero-rated supplies (domestic)
 *   exempt         — Exempt supplies (no VAT, not recoverable)
 *   capital_goods  — Standard-rated capital goods (separate VAT201 box)
 *   export         — Zero-rated exports from RSA
 *   imported       — Imported goods/services (reverse charge for services)
 *   reverse_charge — Domestic reverse charge (DRC VAT)
 *   bad_debt       — Bad debt VAT recovery
 *   no_vat         — No VAT applicable (not a taxable supply)
 */

-- 1. Add vat_type to gl_journal_lines
ALTER TABLE gl_journal_lines
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS vat_type TEXT;

-- 2. Add vat_classification to supplier_invoice_items
ALTER TABLE supplier_invoice_items
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS vat_classification TEXT;

-- 3. Add adjustment_category to vat_adjustments
ALTER TABLE vat_adjustments
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS adjustment_category TEXT
    DEFAULT 'other'
    CHECK (adjustment_category IN ('bad_debt', 'import', 'prior_period', 'change_in_use', 'other'));

-- 4. Default existing VAT journal lines based on GL account
-- Lines to VAT Output (2120) → standard
UPDATE gl_journal_lines jl
SET vat_type = 'standard'

# COMPREHENSIVE ISAFLOW ACCOUNTING MODULE AUDIT

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
ISAFlow is a fully-featured, production-grade accounting system built on Next.js/TypeScript with PostgreSQL. It implements enterprise-grade features comparable to Sage Accounting with South African compliance (SARS, VAT201). The system supports multi-company/group consolidation, approval workflows, bank reconciliation, fixed assets, payroll integration, and AI-powered features.

---

## 1. NAVIGATION & UI STRUCTURE

### Architecture
- **Dual Navigation Modes**: Top-bar (Sage-style, default) and collapsible sidebar
- **User Preference Persistence**: Stored in `localStorage` (`accounting-nav-mode`, `accounting-sidebar-collapsed`)
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile sidebar overlay, desktop sidebar with collapse toggle

### Navigation Files
- `/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx` — Main layout container with PWA install banner, theme toggle, nav mode switcher
- `/src/components/layout/SidebarNav.tsx` — Hierarchical flyout navigation via React portals (prevents clipping)
- `/src/components/layout/ModuleNav.tsx` — Top-bar horizontal navigation with teal accent colors
- `/src/components/accounting/AccountingNav.tsx` — Accounting-specific nav wrapper
- `/src/components/accounting/accountingNavConfig.ts` — Complete tab/menu configuration (13 tabs, nested flyouts)

### Features
- **Breadcrumb-free Navigation**: Semantic link nesting; users always know where they are
- **Quick Actions**: Each tab has `topItems` for rapid access (e.g., "Add a Customer")
- **Company Switcher**: Persistent across all pages, updates X-Company-Id header
- **User Menu**: Name, role, initials avatar, logout button
- **Theme Toggle**: Dark/light mode via ThemeContext
- **PWA Install Banner**: Dismissible, persists preference

### Tab Structure (13 Tabs)
1. **Dashboard** — Overview page
2. **Customers** — AR, quotes, invoices, receipts, credit notes, statements, dunning
3. **Suppliers** — AP, POs, invoices, payments, batch payments, statements
4. **Items** — Inventory, categories, adjustments, pricing, reports
5. **Banking** — Accounts, transactions, reconciliation, transfers, mapping rules, feeds
6. **Accounts** — COA, journals, fiscal periods, currencies, exchange rates
7. **VAT** — Returns, adjustments, DRC VAT
8. **Accountant's Area** — Reports, fixed assets, depreciation, year-end close, budgets
9. **Reports** — Financial (P&L, BS, CF), Management, Transactional
10. **SARS** — VAT201, EMP201, compliance calendar
11. **Tools** — Document capture, approvals, time tracking, company settings, user access
12. **Group** — Multi-entity consolidation, intercompany reconciliation
13. **Payroll** — Employees, runs, leave (cross-module integration)

---

## 2. BANK ALLOCATION & FEATURES

### Bank Account Management

## 14. DATA VALIDATION & ERROR PREVENTION

### Input Validation (Client-Side)
- **Customer Form** (`/components/accounting/CustomerForm.tsx`):
  - Email regex validation: `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`
  - Required fields: name
  - Numeric validation: payment_terms, credit_limit must be numbers
  - Field error display with inline messages

- **Bank Transaction Batch Edit**:
  - Required account selection for allocation type
  - Amount validation (not zero)
  - VAT code validation if applicable

- **Journal Entry Form**:
  - At least 2 lines required
  - Debit/credit balance check
  - GL account required per line
  - Amount validation (>0)

### Data Validation (Server-Side)
- **Chart of Accounts**:
  - Unique account_code constraint (DB level)
  - Valid account_type check (enum constraint)
  - Normal balance must be debit or credit
  - Parent account must exist if specified

- **Fiscal Periods**:
  - Unique (fiscal_year, period_number)
  - Start date < end date
  - Date range validation

- **GL Journal Entries**:
  - Enforce balanced entries on post (trigger function `enforce_balanced_entry()`)
  - No duplicate entry_number (unique constraint)
  - Fiscal period must exist
  - Auto-generate entry_number if null (trigger function `generate_journal_entry_number()`)

- **VAT Adjustments**:
  - Valid adjustment_category enum
  - Amount must be >0
  - Period must exist and be open

- **Approval Rules**:
  - condition_operator must be valid (greater_than, greater_equal, any)
  - document_type must be supported
  - priority defaults to 100

### Error Handling
- **HTTP Status Codes**:
  - 400: Bad request (validation failed)
  - 403: Forbidden (no access to company)
  - 404: Resource not found
  - 500: Server error

- **Error Response Format**:
  ```json
  {
    "success": false,
    "error": {
      "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
      "message": "Account code already exists"
    }
  }
  ```

- **Toast Notifications**: Errors displayed as red toast with message

### Transaction Constraints
- **Double-Entry Accounting**: Debits must equal credits (enforced on post)
- **GL Balance Consistency**: Account balances calculated on every post
- **Period Lock**: Cannot post to closed periods
- **Reversal Only**: Cannot delete posted entries, must reverse

  - `idx_gl_je_source` (source)
  - `idx_gl_je_status` (status)
  - `idx_gl_je_number` (entry_number)

- **GL Journal Lines**:
  - `idx_gl_jl_entry` (journal_entry_id)
  - `idx_gl_jl_account` (gl_account_id)
  - `idx_gl_jl_project` (project_id, WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL)

- **VAT Reporting**:
  - `idx_journal_lines_vat_type` (vat_type, WHERE vat_type IS NOT NULL)
  - `idx_journal_lines_vat_reporting` (gl_account_id, vat_type)

- **User Sessions**:
  - `idx_user_sessions_composite` (id, token_hash, expires_at)
  - Reduced auth lookup from 600ms → 100ms

- **Approval Requests**:
  - `idx_approval_requests_status` (status)
  - `idx_approval_requests_document` (document_type, document_id)

### Pagination
- **Default Page Size**: 25 records per page (adjustable)
- **Offset/Limit**: All list APIs support `limit` and `offset` query params
- **Lazy Loading**: Used in modals (accounts, customers, suppliers)
- **Examples**:
  - `GET /api/accounting/bank-transactions?limit=25&offset=0`
  - `GET /api/accounting/customer-invoices-list?limit=50&offset=0`

### Lazy Loading of Modals
- **Dynamic Import**: Modals loaded on-demand (only when opened)
- **Files**:
  - `SplitTransactionModal`, `FindMatchModal`, `ExcludeReasonModal`
  - `BankTxAttachmentsModal`, `CreateRuleModal`, `CreateEntityModal`
- **Benefit**: Reduces initial page load bundle size

### Caching Strategies
- **No Explicit Redis Cache** (not configured)
- **localStorage**: Nav preferences, theme, UI state
- **In-Memory**: Reference data cached in state (GL accounts, customers, suppliers)
- **DB Caching**: `gl_account_balances` table cache (updated on every post)

### Client-Side Optimization
- **Debounced Search**: 500ms delay on bank transaction search
- **Debounced Rules Preview**: 300ms delay on pattern change
- **Batch Loading**: Promise.all() for parallel reference data requests
- **Memoization**: useMemo() and useCallback() for derived state

---

## ADVANCED FEATURES INVENTORY

### AI/ML Capabilities
- **Smart Categorization** (`smartCategorizationService`): Auto-classify bank txs
- **AI Commentary** (`aiCommentaryService`): Generate narrative summaries
- **Anomaly Detection** (`anomalyDetectionService`): Flag unusual transactions
- **Invoice Pipeline** (`aiInvoicePipelineService`): End-to-end invoice processing
- **Cash Flow AI** (`cashFlowAIService`): Forecast cash position
- **NL Query** (`nlQueryService`): Natural language report queries
- **Report Narrative** (`reportNarrativeService`): Generate written analysis

### Fixed Assets Management
- **Pages**: 
  - `/accounting/assets/index.tsx` — Asset list with search/filter
  - `/accounting/assets/new.tsx` — Create asset
  - `/accounting/assets/register.tsx` — Asset register report
  - `/accounting/assets/disposals.tsx` — Track disposals
  - `/accounting/assets/categories.tsx` — SARS categories

- **Features**:
  - Track purchase date, cost, depreciation method
  - Calculate book value, accumulated depreciation
  - Useful life in years, salvage value
  - Disposals with gain/loss GL postings
  - SARS rate mapping (15%, 20%, 25%, 33%)
  - Asset locations, assignment tracking

### Group Company Consolidation
- **Pages**:
  - `/accounting/group/index.tsx` — Dashboard
  - `/accounting/group/setup.tsx` — Configure entities
  - `/accounting/group/trial-balance.tsx` — Consolidated TB
  - `/accounting/group/income-statement.tsx` — Consolidated P&L
  - `/accounting/group/balance-sheet.tsx` — Consolidated BS
  - `/accounting/group/intercompany.tsx` — Reconciliation
  - `/accounting/group/eliminations.tsx` — Elimination adjustments

- **Features**:
  - Multiple legal entities in single group
  - Consolidated reporting across entities
  - Intercompany transaction tracking
  - Elimination entries (reversals)
  - Proportional consolidation option
  - Currency conversion for foreign entities

### Time Tracking & Project Accounting
- **Pages**: `/accounting/time-tracking/index.tsx`
- **Integration**: Hours tracked → Project revenue calculation
- **Billable Rates**: Per employee, per project
- **Project Profitability**: Actual vs budgeted hours

### Budgeting & Forecasting
- **Budget Management** (`/accounting/budgets/index.tsx`):
  - Annual budgets per GL account
  - Budget copy from prior year
  - Fiscal year selection
  - Variance reporting

- **Cash Flow Forecast** (`/accounting/cash-flow-forecast.tsx`):
  - Historical patterns analysis
  - Recurring invoice projection
  - Known payables integration
  - Seasonal trend modeling
  - Confidence scoring
  - Alert thresholds

- **Scenario Planning** (`scenarioPlanningService`):
  - Multiple forecast scenarios
  - Sensitivity analysis
  - What-if modeling

### Continuous Close
- **Service**: `continuousCloseService`
- **Month-End Close**: `/api/accounting/month-end-close`
- **Features**:
  - Auto-calculate depreciation
  - Accrue known expenses
  - Reconcile intercompany
  - Eliminate inter-entity transactions
  - Generate closing entries

### SARS Compliance
- **VAT201 Filing**: Pre-calculated boxes, direct efiling
- **EMP201**: Payroll tax reconciliation
- **IRP5**: Employee tax certificates
- **Filing Calendar**: Compliance deadline tracking
- **Submission History**: Filed returns with status

### Payment Gateway Integration
- **Service**: `paymentGatewayService`
- **Support**: Multiple payment processors (Stripe, PayU, etc. implied)
- **Reconciliation**: Auto-match gateway deposits to GL

### Bank-Specific Integrations
- **Bank Feeds**: Stitch API integration
- **OFX Import**: Open Financial Exchange format
- **CSV Import**: Configurable mapping
- **PDF Extraction**: Statement PDF parsing

---

## SUMMARY BY MATURITY LEVEL

### Tier 1: Fully Implemented & Production-Ready
- GL accounting (chart, entries, posting, reversal)
- Fiscal period management
- Bank reconciliation (3-way match, rules engine)
- Customer/supplier management
- Invoice & payment processing
- VAT/Tax reporting (VAT201)
- Approval workflows with thresholds
- User access control & role-based security
- Financial reporting (P&L, BS, CF, Trial Balance)
- Fixed assets with depreciation
- Group company consolidation
- Report exports (Excel, CSV, PDF)

### Tier 2: Functional with Minor Gaps
- Inventory/stock management (exists but minimal detail in audit)
- Bank feeds (Stitch integration, needs provider config)
- Document capture (OCR/VLM enabled)
- Audit trail (exists but no detailed change history table)
- Cash flow forecasting (AI-powered, works well)
- Batch payment processing
- Customer/supplier statements
- Aging reports (AR/AP)
- Cost centre allocation

### Tier 3: Partially Implemented
- Project accounting (core exists, profitability tracking)
- Time tracking (pages exist, service layer complete)
- Payroll integration (cross-module, needs payroll module context)
- CRM features (customer/supplier data, but no full CRM)
- Purchase order matching (3-way match framework, not detailed)

### Tier 4: Foundation Only
- Continuous close (service exists, workflows not detailed)
- Scenario planning (service exists, UI not detailed)
- Smart categorization (service exists, ML model integration not detailed)
- Multi-currency (foreign exchange framework exists, limited UI)

---

## DEPLOYMENT & OPERATIONAL NOTES

### Database
- **PostgreSQL**: Neon (serverless) inferred from imports
- **Migrations**: 266 numbered SQL files in `/scripts/migrations/sql/`
- **Performance**: Optimized indexes on hot paths
- **Audit**: Limited (no dedicated audit_log table)

### Authentication
- **JWT Tokens**: In cookie `ff_auth_token` or Authorization header
- **Session Management**: user_sessions table with expiry
- **Company Scoping**: X-Company-Id header enforced

### Scalability
- **Pagination**: Implemented on all list endpoints
- **Lazy Loading**: Frontend modals, API pagination
- **Indexes**: Comprehensive on hot paths
- **Missing**: Redis cache layer

### Monitoring & Logging
- **Logger Service**: `log.error()`, `log.info()` used throughout
- **Not Visible**: Centralized logging aggregation (Sentry, DataDog, etc.)

### File Upload Limits
- **2 MB limit** on bank transaction attachments
- **Document capture**: Likely higher (not specified)

---

## GAPS & RECOMMENDATIONS

### Missing Features
1. **Audit Log Table**: No detailed change history (before/after values)
2. **Excel Import**: No direct Excel import to GL (only export)
3. **Multi-Currency**: Framework exists, limited UI
4. **Custom Fields**: No user-defined fields on entities
5. **Workflow Builder**: Approval rules are basic (no custom workflows)
6. **Mobile App**: Web-only (PWA available)
7. **API Webhooks**: No external integrations via webhooks
8. **Two-Factor Auth**: Not mentioned
9. **Audit Dashboard**: No real-time audit log viewer
10. **Data Retention Policy**: No archival/purge automation

### Performance Improvements
1. Add Redis cache for GL account lookups
2. Implement materialized views for complex reports
3. Add query result caching for static reports
4. Consider read replicas for reporting queries
5. Archive old transactions (>3 years) to separate schema

### Security Enhancements
1. Implement field-level encryption for sensitive data (tax IDs, bank accounts)
2. Add API rate limiting
3. Implement RBAC with more granular permissions (document-level)
4. Add IP whitelisting for admin operations
5. Implement PII masking in logs

### User Experience
1. Add "Undo" for recent transactions
2. Implement draft saves for long forms
3. Add shortcuts panel for power users
4. Implement keyboard navigation in tables
5. Add bulk import/export templates

---

## CONCLUSION

ISAFlow is a **comprehensive, enterprise-grade accounting system** with strong foundations in:
- Double-entry accounting (GL, journal entries, balances)
- Banking integration (Stitch, reconciliation, rules)
- Tax compliance (VAT201, SARS, EMP201)
- Multi-company/group consolidation
- Approval workflows and access control
- Financial reporting and analysis

**Strengths**: Modular architecture, good UI/UX, extensive feature set, South African compliance
**Weaknesses**: Limited audit trail, no multi-currency UI, basic approval rules, missing webhooks
**Readiness**: Production-ready for SMEs and mid-market companies; enterprise features require customization

The codebase is well-organized, performant, and maintainable with clear separation of concerns across pages, APIs, services, and utilities.

# COMPREHENSIVE ISAFLOW ACCOUNTING MODULE AUDIT

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
ISAFlow is a fully-featured, production-grade accounting system built on Next.js/TypeScript with PostgreSQL. It implements enterprise-grade features comparable to Sage Accounting with South African compliance (SARS, VAT201). The system supports multi-company/group consolidation, approval workflows, bank reconciliation, fixed assets, payroll integration, and AI-powered features.

---

## 1. NAVIGATION & UI STRUCTURE

### Architecture
- **Dual Navigation Modes**: Top-bar (Sage-style, default) and collapsible sidebar
- **User Preference Persistence**: Stored in `localStorage` (`accounting-nav-mode`, `accounting-sidebar-collapsed`)
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile sidebar overlay, desktop sidebar with collapse toggle

### Navigation Files
- `/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx` — Main layout container with PWA install banner, theme toggle, nav mode switcher
- `/src/components/layout/SidebarNav.tsx` — Hierarchical flyout navigation via React portals (prevents clipping)
- `/src/components/layout/ModuleNav.tsx` — Top-bar horizontal navigation with teal accent colors
- `/src/components/accounting/AccountingNav.tsx` — Accounting-specific nav wrapper
- `/src/components/accounting/accountingNavConfig.ts` — Complete tab/menu configuration (13 tabs, nested flyouts)

### Features
- **Breadcrumb-free Navigation**: Semantic link nesting; users always know where they are
- **Quick Actions**: Each tab has `topItems` for rapid access (e.g., "Add a Customer")
- **Company Switcher**: Persistent across all pages, updates X-Company-Id header
- **User Menu**: Name, role, initials avatar, logout button
- **Theme Toggle**: Dark/light mode via ThemeContext
- **PWA Install Banner**: Dismissible, persists preference

### Tab Structure (13 Tabs)
1. **Dashboard** — Overview page
2. **Customers** — AR, quotes, invoices, receipts, credit notes, statements, dunning
3. **Suppliers** — AP, POs, invoices, payments, batch payments, statements
4. **Items** — Inventory, categories, adjustments, pricing, reports
5. **Banking** — Accounts, transactions, reconciliation, transfers, mapping rules, feeds
6. **Accounts** — COA, journals, fiscal periods, currencies, exchange rates
7. **VAT** — Returns, adjustments, DRC VAT
8. **Accountant's Area** — Reports, fixed assets, depreciation, year-end close, budgets
9. **Reports** — Financial (P&L, BS, CF), Management, Transactional
10. **SARS** — VAT201, EMP201, compliance calendar
11. **Tools** — Document capture, approvals, time tracking, company settings, user access
12. **Group** — Multi-entity consolidation, intercompany reconciliation
13. **Payroll** — Employees, runs, leave (cross-module integration)

---

## 2. BANK ALLOCATION & FEATURES

### Bank Account Management
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/bank-accounts/index.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - List/add bank accounts linked to GL chart
  - Display debit/credit totals, running balance
  - Mask account numbers (show last 4 digits only)
  - Track first/last transaction dates
  - Link to GL via account code + account subtype='bank'

### Bank Transaction Processing
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/bank-transactions/index.tsx` (700+ lines)
- **Features**:
  - **Tab-based Views**: New (imported), Reviewed (matched), Excluded
  - **Search**: Debounced 500ms server-side search on description/reference
  - **Date Range Filtering**: From/to dates with date pickers
  - **Amount Range Filtering**: Min/max transaction amount
  - **Batch Edit**: 
    - Allocate to GL accounts, suppliers, customers, cost centers
    - Live filtering/autocomplete for options
  - **Lazy-loaded Modals**: SplitTransactionModal, FindMatchModal, ExcludeReasonModal, AttachmentsModal, CreateRuleModal
  - **Export**: CSV/Excel via `/api/accounting/bank-transactions-export`
  - **Reconciliation Status**: Displays balance, unreconciled count, unrec balance

### Bank Reconciliation
- **Files**:
  - `/pages/accounting/bank-reconciliation/index.tsx` — Main reconciliation
  - `/pages/accounting/bank-reconciliation/[reconId].tsx` — Recon detail
  - `/pages/accounting/bank-reconciliation/rules.tsx` — Bank categorization rules
  - `/pages/accounting/bank-reconciliation/import.tsx` — Statement import (CSV/OFX/QIF/PDF)
- **Features**:
  - **3-Way Match**: Bank statement + GL + supplier invoice reconciliation
  - **Auto-Matching**: Fuzzy match on amount + payee, support for split transactions
  - **Rules Engine**: Pattern matching (description contains/exact/regex), priority-based
  - **Match Candidates API**: Suggests matches with confidence scores
  - **Split Transactions**: Allocate one bank tx to multiple GL lines
  - **Exclusion Reasons**: Document why txs are excluded
  - **Statement Import Formats**: CSV, OFX, QIF, PDF (bank statement extraction)

### Bank Feeds Integration
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/bank-feeds.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - **Provider**: Stitch (live bank connection)
  - **Sync History**: Track fetches, imports, skips, errors per connection
  - **Status Tracking**: Synced/syncing/pending/error states
  - **Manual Sync**: Trigger on-demand sync per connection
  - **Sync Logs**: Detailed transaction log with timestamps
  - **Auto-Import**: Transactions pulled directly from bank API

### Bank Rules/Categorization
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/bank-reconciliation/rules.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - **Rule Types**: Match field (description, reference, amount), match type (contains, exact, regex)
  - **Actions**: Allocate to GL account, supplier, customer; apply VAT code
  - **Priority-Based**: Rules execute in priority order (default 100)
  - **Description Template**: Auto-generate description from pattern captures
  - **Auto-Create Entry**: Checkbox to auto-post GL entry on match
  - **Live Preview**: Hover shows match count for pattern
  - **Bulk Delete**: Select multiple rules for deletion

### Bank API Endpoints
- `GET /api/accounting/bank-accounts` — List bank accounts with balances
- `GET /api/accounting/bank-transactions` — List with pagination (limit/offset), search, date range, amount range
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-transactions-action` — Mark reviewed, delete, exclude
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-transactions-import` — Bulk import from file
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-transactions-manual` — Manual entry
- `GET /api/accounting/bank-reconciliations` — List reconciliation runs
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-match-candidates` — Get match suggestions
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-match-confirm` — Confirm a match
- `GET /api/accounting/bank-rules` — List categorization rules
- `POST /api/accounting/bank-rules-action` — Create/update/delete rules
- `GET /api/accounting/bank-rules-preview` — Preview rule matches

---

## 3. SEARCH FUNCTIONALITY

### Global Account Search
- **Debounced 500ms server-side search** across bank transactions
- **Search Fields**: Description, reference, narrative (for bank tx)
- **Parameters**: `?search=term&limit=25&offset=0`

### Account Number & Name Search
- **Chart of Accounts**: Indexed by code (`idx_gl_accounts_code`) and type
- **Bank Transactions**: Search by account code OR account name
- **References**: Most list pages include filtering/autocomplete for accounts

### Customer/Supplier Search
- **Autocomplete**: Real-time filtering for allocation modals
- **Parameters**: Optional `?q=searchterm` or pattern matching
- **Case-Insensitive**: Leverages database ILIKE

### Bank Rules Pattern Preview
- **Live Preview Count**: Shows how many transactions match pattern
- **Debounced Updates**: 300ms delay on pattern change
- **Match Types**: contains, exact, regex support

### Advanced Filters
- **Date Range**: From/to filters with date pickers
- **Status Filters**: Account status, reconciliation status, transaction status
- **Amount Range**: Min/max filters with number input
- **Cost Centre**: Filter by cc1/cc2/department
- **Entity Type**: Filter customer vs supplier transactions

---

## 4. VAT/TAX REPORTING

### VAT Framework
- **File**: `/scripts/migrations/sql/210_vat201_data_model.sql`
- **VAT Types** (8 classification types):
  - `standard` — 15% standard rate supplies/purchases
  - `zero_rated` — 0% zero-rated supplies (domestic)
  - `exempt` — Exempt supplies (no VAT, not recoverable)
  - `capital_goods` — Standard-rated capital goods
  - `export` — Zero-rated exports from RSA
  - `imported` — Imported goods/services (reverse charge)
  - `reverse_charge` — Domestic reverse charge (DRC VAT)
  - `bad_debt` — Bad debt VAT recovery
  - `no_vat` — Not a taxable supply

### VAT211 Data Model
- **gl_journal_lines.vat_type** — Classify lines by VAT type
- **supplier_invoice_items.vat_classification** — Classify supplier invoice items
- **vat_adjustments.adjustment_category** — Track adjustment reason (bad_debt, import, prior_period, change_in_use, other)
- **Index on (gl_account_id, vat_type)** — Fast VAT reporting queries

### VAT Return Reporting
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/reports/vat-return.tsx`
- **API**: `GET /api/accounting/reports-vat-return?period_start=YYYY-MM-DD&period_end=YYYY-MM-DD`
- **Features**:
  - **VAT201 Box Mapping**: Automatic calculation of boxes 1-8 (output, input, DRC, etc.)
  - **Period-Based Calculation**: Monthly/quarterly periods
  - **Export**: CSV/Excel via `/api/accounting/vat-return-export`
  - **Comparative Reports**: Compare prior periods
  - **Bad Debt Recovery**: Automatic VAT recovery for write-offs
  - **Reverse Charge Tracking**: DRC VAT separate calculation

### VAT Adjustments
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/vat-adjustments/index.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - **Adjustment Types**: Bad debt, import/export, prior period, change in use
  - **Post to GL**: Auto-generates GL entries for adjustments
  - **VAT Recovery**: Track recoverable vs non-recoverable
  - **Period Mapping**: Assign to specific fiscal period
  - **Approval**: Optional approval workflow for adjustments >R5k

### DRC VAT (Domestic Reverse Charge)
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/drc-vat.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - Track DRC transactions separately
  - Calculate VAT on DRC supplies
  - Report DRC in VAT201 Box 7

### SARS Filing
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/sars/vat201.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - **Pre-filled VAT201 Forms**: Auto-calculate all boxes
  - **Submission History**: Track filed returns
  - **E-filing**: Direct integration (if SARS efiling service configured)
  - **Status Tracking**: Submitted/accepted/rejected

---

## 5. AUDIT TRAILS & HISTORY TRACKING

### Database Audit Logging
- **No explicit audit table** in schema (checked 200_accounting_foundation.sql)
- **GL Entry Tracking**:
  - `gl_journal_entries.created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - `posted_by`, `posted_at` — Manual post tracking
  - `reversed_by`, `reversed_at` — Reversal tracking
  - `source` field (manual, auto_invoice, auto_payment, auto_bank_recon, auto_credit_note)
  - `status` field (draft, posted, reversed)

### Audit Report Page
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/reports/audit-trail.tsx`
- **Features**:
  - List all GL entries by date range
  - Filter by account code, entry type, status
  - Show who posted/reversed and when
  - Export capability

### Transaction History
- **Bank Transactions**: Track status changes (imported → matched/excluded)
- **Customer Invoices**: Status progression (draft → posted → paid/write-off)
- **Supplier Invoices**: Track approval status
- **Approval Requests**: Full decision audit (requested_at, decided_by, decided_at, notes)

### User Session Tracking
- **File**: `/src/lib/auth/middleware.ts`
- **user_sessions table**: Token hash, expires_at
- **Composite Index**: `idx_user_sessions_composite(id, token_hash, expires_at)` for performance

### Missing Features
- No timestamped `audit_log` table with operation/user/timestamp/change details
- No change history (before/after values) for GL accounts, customer data, etc.
- Could benefit from event sourcing pattern for full transaction history

---

## 6. TRANSACTION CONTROLS & APPROVAL WORKFLOWS

### Approval Workflow Engine
- **File**: `/scripts/migrations/sql/234_approval_workflows.sql`
- **Features**:
  - **Rule-Based Thresholds**: Approval required if amount > threshold
  - **Document Types Supported**: Customer invoice, supplier invoice, payment, journal entry, credit note
  - **Approver Roles**: admin, manager, accountant (configurable)
  - **Condition Operators**: greater_than, greater_equal, any
  - **Priority-Based**: Execute rules in priority order (lower = higher priority)

### Default Rules (Pre-seeded)
- Large customer invoices >R50k → manager approval
- Large supplier invoices >R50k → manager approval
- Large payments >R100k → admin approval
- All journal entries → accountant approval
- Credit notes >R10k → manager approval

### Approval Request Lifecycle
- **File**: `/pages/accounting/approvals/index.tsx`
- **Status States**: pending, approved, rejected, cancelled
- **Fields**:
  - Document type, document ID, reference (INV-001, JE-042)
  - Amount, requested_by, requested_at
  - decided_by, decided_at, decision_notes
  - Created audit record

### Approval Request APIs
- `GET /api/accounting/approval-requests` — List pending/history

## 14. DATA VALIDATION & ERROR PREVENTION

### Input Validation (Client-Side)
- **Customer Form** (`/components/accounting/CustomerForm.tsx`):
  - Email regex validation: `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`
  - Required fields: name
  - Numeric validation: payment_terms, credit_limit must be numbers
  - Field error display with inline messages

- **Bank Transaction Batch Edit**:
  - Required account selection for allocation type
  - Amount validation (not zero)
  - VAT code validation if applicable

- **Journal Entry Form**:
  - At least 2 lines required
  - Debit/credit balance check
  - GL account required per line
  - Amount validation (>0)

### Data Validation (Server-Side)
- **Chart of Accounts**:
  - Unique account_code constraint (DB level)
  - Valid account_type check (enum constraint)
  - Normal balance must be debit or credit
  - Parent account must exist if specified

- **Fiscal Periods**:
  - Unique (fiscal_year, period_number)
  - Start date < end date
  - Date range validation

- **GL Journal Entries**:
  - Enforce balanced entries on post (trigger function `enforce_balanced_entry()`)
  - No duplicate entry_number (unique constraint)
  - Fiscal period must exist
  - Auto-generate entry_number if null (trigger function `generate_journal_entry_number()`)

- **VAT Adjustments**:
  - Valid adjustment_category enum
  - Amount must be >0
  - Period must exist and be open

- **Approval Rules**:
  - condition_operator must be valid (greater_than, greater_equal, any)
  - document_type must be supported
  - priority defaults to 100

### Error Handling
- **HTTP Status Codes**:
  - 400: Bad request (validation failed)
  - 403: Forbidden (no access to company)
  - 404: Resource not found
  - 500: Server error

- **Error Response Format**:
  ```json
  {
    "success": false,
    "error": {
      "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
      "message": "Account code already exists"
    }
  }
  ```

- **Toast Notifications**: Errors displayed as red toast with message

### Transaction Constraints
- **Double-Entry Accounting**: Debits must equal credits (enforced on post)
- **GL Balance Consistency**: Account balances calculated on every post
- **Period Lock**: Cannot post to closed periods
- **Reversal Only**: Cannot delete posted entries, must reverse

Here's my analysis comparing your partner's feedback against what ISAFlow actually has:

---

## VERDICT: ISAFlow is Strong — But There Are Real Gaps

Your partner's 45 years of experience shows. His concerns are exactly the pain points that separate "software that works" from "software accountants love." Here's how we stack up:

---

### 1. Usability and Complexity — **STRONG**

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| Unintuitive interfaces | **Addressed** — Dual nav (top-bar + sidebar), 13 organized tabs, quick actions per section |
| Steep learning curves | **Partially addressed** — Good structure, but no onboarding tour, no tooltips, no contextual help |
| Complex navigation | **Addressed** — Flyout menus, company switcher, breadcrumb-style nesting |

**Gaps to fix:**
- No keyboard shortcuts panel for power users (accountants live on keyboards)
- No contextual help / "What's this?" tooltips
- No guided onboarding tour for first-time users

---

### 2. System Integration — **GOOD, with gaps**

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| Banking integration | **Strong** — Stitch bank feeds, OFX/CSV/QIF/PDF import, auto-matching |
| Payroll integration | **Exists** — Cross-module nav, GL posting from payroll runs |
| CRM integration | **Weak** — Customer/supplier data exists but no dedicated CRM |
| Inventory integration | **Exists** — Items module with movement tracking, valuations |

**Gaps to fix:**
- No webhook/API integration for third-party CRM systems
- No direct bank-to-bank payment initiation (only reconciliation)

---

### 3. Data Accuracy and Error Risks — **STRONG**

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| Input errors cascading | **Well-guarded** — DB-level constraints enforce balanced entries, debit/credit checks, period locks |
| Reconciliation accuracy | **Strong** — 3-way matching, confidence scoring, split transactions |

**Gaps to fix:**
- **No detailed audit log table** — This is the biggest gap your partner would care about. We track who posted/reversed, but not field-level change history (before/after values). A veteran accountant expects to see "User X changed invoice amount from R50,000 to R55,000 at 14:32"
- No "undo last action" feature

---

### 4. Performance and Reliability — **GOOD**

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| System lag | **Optimized** — Pagination, lazy-loaded modals, debounced search, composite indexes |
| Crashes/bugs | **11 known bugs fixed** per E2E testing |

**Gaps to fix:**
- No Redis caching layer — report queries on large datasets will slow down
- No materialized views for complex reports (consolidated group reporting will get slow)

---

### 5. Reporting and Compliance — **VERY STRONG**

This is where ISAFlow shines. Your partner would approve.

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| Inflexible reporting | **Strong** — P&L, BS, Cash Flow, Trial Balance, Budget vs Actual, aging reports, drill-down |
| Real-time insights | **Yes** — Live calculations, period-based filtering, comparative reports |
| VAT compliance | **Excellent** — Full VAT201 box mapping, DRC VAT, bad debt recovery, SARS efiling |
| IFRS compliance | **Partial** — Standard financials exist, but no explicit IFRS disclosure notes |

**Gaps to fix:**
- No IFRS disclosure note generator
- No custom report builder (users can't create their own report layouts)

---

### 6. Customer Support and Cost — **N/A** (product-level, not code)

This is a business model question, not a feature gap. Worth noting his concern about subscription fatigue — ISAFlow's self-hosted model is actually an advantage here.

---

### 7. Migration and Vendor Lock-in — **GOOD**

| His Concern | ISAFlow Status |
|---|---|
| Data transfer | **Strong** — Sage migration tool built-in, CSV/OFX import |
| Export functionality | **16+ export endpoints** — Excel, CSV, PDF across all modules |
| Vendor lock-in | **Low risk** — PostgreSQL, standard data model, comprehensive exports |

---

### 8. Cloud vs Desktop — **HYBRID ADVANTAGE**

ISAFlow is self-hosted but web-accessible — best of both worlds. PWA support adds mobile capability.

---

### Now the Practical Improvements — His Specific Requests:

| His Request | ISAFlow Status | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| **Bank allocation streamlining** | **Done** — Rules engine, auto-matching, split transactions, batch edit | -- |
| **Search by account name AND number** | **Done** — ILIKE search on both fields | -- |
| **Simplified navigation with shortcuts** | **Partial** — Good nav structure, but NO keyboard shortcuts | **HIGH** |
| **VAT and audit support** | **VAT: Excellent. Audit: WEAK** — No field-level change history | **CRITICAL** |
| **Transaction thresholds** | **Done** — Approval workflows with configurable thresholds (R50k invoices, R100k payments) | -- |
| **Button-driven interface** | **Done** — Modern React UI with buttons, not menu-driven | -- |
| **Account mapping to financials** | **Done** — Account type/subtype auto-routes to correct statement | -- |
| **Granular user access** | **Partial** — 4 roles (owner/admin/manager/viewer), but no field-level or document-level permissions | **MEDIUM** |
| **Period selection** | **Done** — Fiscal periods with open/closing/closed/locked states | -- |
| **Comprehensive reporting** | **Done** — Full suite including cash flow | -- |
| **Excel exports without merged cells** | **Done** — Server-side generation, analysis-ready format | -- |
| **Debit/credit display toggle** | **NOT DONE** — Separate columns for journals, but no user toggle for net vs split view | **MEDIUM** |

---

## TOP 5 PRIORITIES Based on His Feedback

1. **Proper Audit Trail Table** (CRITICAL) — A 45-year accountant's #1 requirement. We need a dedicated `audit_log` table that captures: who, what, when, old value, new value, for every change to financial data. This is non-negotiable for any serious accounting firm.

2. **Keyboard Shortcuts** (HIGH) — Power users (accountants) navigate with keyboards. We need: Ctrl+N (new entry), Ctrl+S (save), Tab navigation in grids, account code auto-complete on type, shortcut panel (? key).

3. **Debit/Credit Display Toggle** (MEDIUM) — Let users choose between separate debit/credit columns or a single net amount column. Different accountants prefer different views.

4. **Granular Permissions** (MEDIUM) — Expand beyond 4 roles to include: read-only on specific modules, posting rights per account range, approval-only access, report-only access.

5. **IFRS Disclosure Notes** (MEDIUM) — For compliance-conscious firms, auto-generate standard IFRS disclosure notes from the financials data.

---

## My Opinion

Your partner's analysis is spot-on and well-organized. The good news: **ISAFlow already addresses roughly 70-75% of his concerns**, particularly the core accounting, banking, VAT, and reporting areas. The areas where we're weak — audit trails, keyboard shortcuts, granular permissions — are exactly the things that differentiate "developer-built accounting software" from "accountant-approved accounting software."

The audit trail gap is the most urgent. No experienced accountant will trust a system where they can't trace exactly who changed what and when. That should be our next major feature.

Want me to start implementing any of these? The audit trail table would be the highest-impact improvement.

## Existing Patterns

Read existing admin services/routes/pages for patterns. Key points:
- Services: `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon';`, `import { log } from '@/lib/logger';`, tagged templates only
- API routes: `withAuth(withRole('super_admin')(withErrorHandler(handler as any) as any) as any)`
- Pages: `AdminLayout` wrapper, `apiFetch` for data, Tailwind + dark mode
- Audit: `logAdminAction(adminUserId, action, targetType, targetId, details, ipAddress)` from `@/modules/admin/services/auditService`

## Existing Database (already migrated)

**system_announcements** — id, title, message, type (info/warning/maintenance/feature), target (all/plan/company), target_ids (UUID[]), starts_at, ends_at, is_dismissible, created_by, created_at

**admin_audit_log** — already exists

## Files to Create

### 1. `src/modules/admin/services/announcementService.ts`

Functions:
- `listAnnouncements(filters?: { active_only?: boolean; page?: number; limit?: number }): Promise<PaginatedResult<Announcement>>` — list all, optionally filter to only currently active (starts_at <= NOW and (ends_at IS NULL or ends_at >= NOW))
- `getAnnouncement(id: string): Promise<Announcement | null>`
- `createAnnouncement(data: { title: string; message: string; type?: string; target?: string; target_ids?: string[]; starts_at: string; ends_at?: string; is_dismissible?: boolean; created_by: string }): Promise<string>` — return id
- `updateAnnouncement(id: string, data: Partial<Announcement>): Promise<void>`
- `deleteAnnouncement(id: string): Promise<void>` — hard delete

Add `Announcement` type to `src/modules/admin/types/admin.types.ts`:
```typescript
export interface Announcement {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  message: string;
  type: string;
  target: string;
  target_ids: string[];
  starts_at: string;
  ends_at: string | null;
  is_dismissible: boolean;
  created_by: string;
  created_at: string;
}
```

### 2. `src/modules/admin/services/impersonationService.ts`

Functions:
- `createImpersonationToken(adminUserId: string, companyId: string): Promise<{ token: string; expires_at: string }>` — generates a JWT with: `{ sub: adminUserId, impersonating: true, company_id: companyId, exp: 30 minutes }`. Use the same JWT secret from env (read how existing auth does it — check `src/lib/auth/` for JWT signing).
- `validateImpersonationToken(token: string): Promise<{ admin_user_id: string; company_id: string } | null>` — verify and decode

Read existing JWT creation in `src/lib/auth/` to use the same `jsonwebtoken` library and secret pattern.

### 3. `src/modules/admin/services/dataExportService.ts`

Functions:
- `exportCompanyData(companyId: string): Promise<{ filename: string; data: Record<string, unknown[]> }>` — queries all major tables scoped to company_id and returns them as a structured object. Tables to export:
  - Company profile (from companies table)
  - Chart of accounts (gl_accounts)
  - Customers (customers)
  - Suppliers (suppliers)
  - Invoices (invoices)
  - Journal entries (gl_journal_entries)
  - Bank transactions (bank_transactions)
  
  Return as `{ filename: 'export-{companyName}-{date}.json', data: { company: [...], accounts: [...], ... } }`

  Note: This returns JSON data. Actual ZIP/CSV generation is a future enhancement — for now return structured JSON.

### 4. API Routes

**`pages/api/admin/announcements.ts`**
- GET: `listAnnouncements(filters)` with query params active_only, page, limit
- POST: parse body, `createAnnouncement({...body, created_by: req.user.id})`, audit log

**`pages/api/admin/announcements/[id].ts`**
- GET: `getAnnouncement(id)`, 404 if null
- PATCH: parse body, `updateAnnouncement(id, body)`, audit log
- DELETE: `deleteAnnouncement(id)`, audit log

**`pages/api/admin/companies/[id]/impersonate.ts`**
- POST: `createImpersonationToken(req.user.id, companyId)`, audit log `company.impersonate`, return token + expires_at

**`pages/api/admin/companies/[id]/export-data.ts`**
- GET: `exportCompanyData(companyId)`, audit log `company.export_data`, return JSON response with Content-Disposition header

**`pages/api/announcements/active.ts`** — Customer-facing, NOT admin-only
- GET: Return active announcements for the current user's company. Use `withCompany`. Query system_announcements WHERE starts_at <= NOW AND (ends_at IS NULL OR ends_at >= NOW) AND (target = 'all' OR (target = 'company' AND company_id = ANY(target_ids))). Also check plan-targeted announcements via company's plan_id.

### 5. UI Pages

**`pages/admin/tools/announcements.tsx`**
- List all announcements in a table: Title, Type (badge), Target, Starts, Ends, Dismissible, Actions
- Create button → modal form with: title, message (textarea), type dropdown, target dropdown (all/plan/company), target_ids (text input, comma-separated UUIDs), starts_at (datetime-local), ends_at (datetime-local, optional), is_dismissible checkbox
- Edit button per row → same modal pre-filled
- Delete button with confirmation
- Type badges: info=blue, warning=yellow, maintenance=orange, feature=green

**`pages/admin/tools/index.tsx`**
- Tools landing page with cards linking to:
  - Sage Auto-Import → /accounting/migration/sage-auto (existing location, with note "Opens in customer app")
  - Announcements → /admin/tools/announcements
  - Data Export → described inline, "Use company detail page → Export Data button"
  - Impersonation → described inline, "Use company detail page → Impersonate button"

### 6. Update AdminNav

Read `src/components/admin/AdminNav.tsx` and update the Tools section to be active (not disabled/coming soon) with sub-links:
- Tools Overview → /admin/tools
- Announcements → /admin/tools/announcements

### 7. `src/components/admin/ImpersonationBanner.tsx`

Banner shown at top of app when admin is impersonating:
```tsx
// Checks for impersonation cookie/flag
// Shows: "You are viewing as [Company Name] — Exit"
// Exit button clears impersonation and redirects to admin
```
Simple component — read from a cookie or localStorage flag.

Create Phase 5: Monitoring & Analytics for ISAFlow Admin Platform. This is the final phase.

## Existing Patterns

Read existing admin services at `src/modules/admin/services/adminDashboardService.ts` for patterns:
- `import { sql } from '@/lib/neon';`
- `import { log } from '@/lib/logger';`
- `type Row = any` with eslint disable
- Tagged template literals only

Read existing admin API routes at `pages/api/admin/dashboard-stats.ts` for the export pattern.
Read existing admin pages at `pages/admin/index.tsx` for UI patterns.
Read `src/components/admin/AdminNav.tsx` for nav structure.

## Files to Create

### 1. Add types to `src/modules/admin/types/admin.types.ts`

Append:

```typescript
export interface PlatformHealth {
  active_users_24h: number;
  active_users_7d: number;
  active_users_30d: number;
  total_api_calls_24h: number;
  error_count_24h: number;
  error_rate_percent: number;
  db_size_mb: number;
  top_companies_by_size: Array<{ company_id: string; company_name: string; size_mb: number }>;
}

export interface UsageAnalytics {
  dau: number;
  wau: number;
  mau: number;
  stickiness_percent: number;
  top_pages: Array<{ path: string; views: number }>;
  feature_adoption: Array<{ feature: string; adoption_percent: number; user_count: number }>;
  revenue_by_plan: Array<{ plan_name: string; mrr_cents: number; company_count: number }>;
  churn_signals: Array<{ company_id: string; company_name: string; days_inactive: number; last_login: string | null }>;
}

export interface PlatformSettings {
  maintenance_mode: boolean;
  registration_enabled: boolean;
  default_trial_days: number;
  max_companies_per_user: number;
  smtp_configured: boolean;
}
```

### 2. `src/modules/admin/services/analyticsService.ts`

Functions:

- `getPlatformHealth(): Promise<PlatformHealth>` — Parallel queries:
  - Active users: COUNT DISTINCT users with last_login in 24h, 7d, 30d
  - API calls: COUNT from admin_audit_log in 24h (proxy for API activity)
  - Error count: COUNT from admin_audit_log WHERE action LIKE 'error%' in 24h (or just 0 if no error tracking yet)
  - DB size: Use `SELECT pg_database_size(current_database())` to get total DB size in MB
  - Top companies by row count: Count rows in major tables (gl_journal_entries, invoices, bank_transactions) grouped by company_id, JOIN companies for name, LIMIT 10

- `getUsageAnalytics(): Promise<UsageAnalytics>` — Parallel queries:
  - DAU/WAU/MAU: COUNT DISTINCT users with last_login in 1d/7d/30d
  - Stickiness: DAU/MAU * 100
  - Top pages: Not trackable without analytics table — return empty array with a comment noting this needs a page_views table
  - Feature adoption: For each feature flag, count companies that have access (via plan or override) / total companies * 100
  - Revenue by plan: JOIN subscriptions + plans, SUM monthly amounts grouped by plan, count companies
  - Churn signals: Companies with no user login in >14 days, ordered by days_inactive DESC, LIMIT 20

- `getPlatformSettings(): Promise<PlatformSettings>` — Read from a `platform_settings` key-value approach. For MVP, return sensible defaults since we don't have a settings table yet:
  ```typescript
  return {
    maintenance_mode: false,
    registration_enabled: true,
    default_trial_days: 14,
    max_companies_per_user: 5,
    smtp_configured: !!process.env.SMTP_HOST || !!process.env.RESEND_API_KEY,
  };
  ```

- `updatePlatformSettings(data: Partial<PlatformSettings>): Promise<void>` — For MVP, log that settings were updated but note there's no persistence table yet. Just log the action.

### 3. API Routes

**`pages/api/admin/analytics/health.ts`**
- GET: `getPlatformHealth()`

**`pages/api/admin/analytics/usage.ts`**
- GET: `getUsageAnalytics()`

**`pages/api/admin/settings.ts`**
- GET: `getPlatformSettings()`

-- Migration 265: Admin Platform — System announcements
-- Allows ISAFlow admins to broadcast messages to all companies, specific plans,
-- or individual companies (maintenance windows, new features, warnings).

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS system_announcements (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  message TEXT NOT NULL,
  type VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'info' CHECK (type IN ('info', 'warning', 'maintenance', 'feature')),
  target VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'all' CHECK (target IN ('all', 'plan', 'company')),
  target_ids UUID[] DEFAULT '{}',
  starts_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  ends_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  is_dismissible BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_by UUID NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

# PRD: ISAFlow Rolls-Royce Roadmap
## Addressing Mr Marneweck's Gap Analysis — Full Implementation Plan

**Version:** 1.0
**Date:** 30 March 2026
**Status:** Draft
**Owner:** ISAFlow Product & Engineering

---

## 1. Overview

This PRD defines the complete implementation plan for every gap and partial item identified in the ISAFlow Gap Analysis Report. It covers 22 deliverables across 4 quarters, organized into 8 workstreams. Each feature includes requirements, acceptance criteria, database changes, API contracts, UI specifications, and testing strategy.

**Goal:** Transform ISAFlow from a strong accounting platform (69% feature coverage) into a Rolls-Royce-class system (100% coverage) that surpasses Sage, Xero, and QuickBooks in the South African market.

---

## 2. Workstream Summary

| # | Workstream | Quarter | Items | Priority |
|---|-----------|---------|-------|----------|
| WS-1 | Audit Trail & Data Integrity | Q2 2026 | 2 | Critical + Medium |
| WS-2 | Security & Authentication | Q2 2026 | 1 | High |
| WS-3 | Command Palette & Keyboard Shortcuts | Q2 2026 | 2 | High |
| WS-4 | Permissions & Governance | Q3 2026 | 2 | High |
| WS-5 | Performance & Caching | Q3 2026 | 1 | High |
| WS-6 | UX Enhancements | Q3 2026 | 6 | Medium |
| WS-7 | Reporting & Compliance | Q4 2026 | 4 | High + Medium |
| WS-8 | Integration & Migration | Q4 2026 + Q1 2027 | 4 | Medium + Low |

---

## 3. Architecture Conventions

All implementations MUST follow existing ISAFlow patterns:

- **Migrations:** `scripts/migrations/sql/NNN_description.sql` — sequential numbering, idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`), indexes on query paths
- **Services:** `src/modules/accounting/services/*Service.ts` — async functions, `sql` tagged templates, `log` singleton, company-scoped queries
- **APIs:** `pages/api/accounting/*.ts` — `withCompany(withErrorHandler(handler))`, `apiResponse.*` helpers, userId from JWT
- **Pages:** `pages/accounting/*.tsx` — `<AppLayout>`, `useCompany()`, `apiFetch()`, hydration safety, Tailwind + CSS vars
- **Preferences:** `user_preferences` table — key/value per user, no company scope
- **Logging:** `log.info/warn/error(message, data, component)` — never `console.*`

---

## WS-1: Audit Trail & Data Integrity (Q2 2026) — CRITICAL

### Feature 1.1: Comprehensive Audit Trail

**Gap:** No field-level change history. Only created_by/posted_by/reversed_by timestamps on GL entries. Accountants need to trace exactly who changed what and when.

**Priority:** Critical
**Effort:** 2 weeks

#### 1.1.1 Database Migration — `267_audit_trail.sql`

```sql
-- Core audit log table
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  company_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  user_email VARCHAR(255),
  action VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (action IN (
    'create', 'update', 'delete', 'post', 'reverse', 'approve', 'reject', 'login', 'export'
  )),
  entity_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  entity_id UUID NOT NULL,
  entity_ref VARCHAR(100),
  changes JSONB,
  ip_address VARCHAR(45),
  user_agent TEXT,
  session_id UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Indexes for common query patterns
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_company ON audit_log(company_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_entity ON audit_log(entity_type, entity_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_user ON audit_log(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_date ON audit_log(created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_action ON audit_log(action);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_company_date ON audit_log(company_id, created_at DESC);

-- GIN index for JSONB changes queries
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_changes ON audit_log USING GIN (changes);
```

**`changes` JSONB structure:**
```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "field": "amount",
      "old": "50000.00",
      "new": "55000.00",
      "label": "Invoice Amount"
    },
    {
      "field": "status",
      "old": "draft",
      "new": "posted",
      "label": "Status"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "source": "manual",
    "reason": "Correction per client request"
  }
}
```

**Entity types to track:**
- `gl_journal_entry` — create, post, reverse
- `gl_account` — create, update, deactivate
- `customer_invoice` — create, update, post, write_off
- `supplier_invoice` — create, update, post, approve
- `bank_transaction` — match, exclude, split, allocate
- `bank_rule` — create, update, delete
- `customer` — create, update, delete
- `supplier` — create, update, delete
- `item` — create, update, delete
- `approval_request` — approve, reject
- `fixed_asset` — create, update, dispose, depreciate
- `budget` — create, update
- `company_settings` — update
- `user_access` — invite, role_change, remove

#### 1.1.2 Service — `auditTrailService.ts`

```
Location: src/modules/accounting/services/auditTrailService.ts

Functions:
  logAudit(params: AuditEntry): Promise<void>
    - Fire-and-forget (non-blocking, catch errors silently)
    - Auto-detect IP from request headers (x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip)
    - Compute diff between old and new objects for 'update' actions

  getAuditLog(companyId, filters): Promise<{ items: AuditLogItem[], total: number }>
    - Filters: entity_type, entity_id, user_id, action, date_from, date_to
    - Pagination: limit, offset
    - Sort: created_at DESC (default)

  getEntityHistory(companyId, entityType, entityId): Promise<AuditLogItem[]>
    - Full change timeline for a specific record
    - Used for "History" panel on entity detail pages

  diffObjects(oldObj, newObj, fieldLabels): ChangeField[]
    - Compute field-level changes
    - Skip unchanged fields
    - Map field names to human-readable labels
    - Handle nested objects (e.g., line items)
```

#### 1.1.3 Integration Pattern

Every service function that modifies data must call `logAudit()` after successful mutation. Pattern:

```typescript
// In journalEntryService.ts → postEntry():
const result = await sql`UPDATE gl_journal_entries SET status='posted' ...`;
await logAudit({
  companyId, userId, action: 'post',
  entityType: 'gl_journal_entry', entityId: id,
  entityRef: result.entry_number,
  changes: { fields: [{ field: 'status', old: 'draft', new: 'posted', label: 'Status' }] },
  ip, userAgent, sessionId,
});
```

#### 1.1.4 API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/accounting/audit-log` | List audit entries with filters, pagination |
| GET | `/api/accounting/audit-log-entity?type=X&id=Y` | History for specific entity |
| GET | `/api/accounting/audit-log-export` | Export audit log as Excel/CSV |

**Query params for list:** `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `user_id`, `action`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `search` (searches entity_ref and user_email), `limit`, `offset`

#### 1.1.5 UI — Audit Log Viewer

**Page:** `pages/accounting/audit-log.tsx`

**Layout:**
- Header: "Audit Trail" title with export button

### Feature 1.2: Undo Capability for Recent Actions

**Gap:** No general undo. Only GL reversals exist for posted entries.

**Priority:** Medium
**Effort:** 1 week

#### 1.2.1 Design

Implement a **soft-delete with undo window** pattern for non-posted transactions:

- When a user deletes a draft invoice, bank rule, customer, supplier, or item → mark as `deleted_at = NOW()` instead of hard delete
- Show toast notification: "Deleted [Entity]. Undo?" with 30-second timer
- If user clicks Undo → clear `deleted_at` timestamp
- Background job purges records where `deleted_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 seconds'`
- All list queries add `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`

#### 1.2.2 Database Migration — `268_soft_delete.sql`

```sql
-- Add soft-delete columns to entities that support undo
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE suppliers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE items ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE bank_rules ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE customer_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE supplier_invoices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

-- Partial indexes for efficient queries (only non-deleted rows)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_customers_active ON customers(company_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_suppliers_active ON suppliers(company_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_items_active ON items(company_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```

#### 1.2.3 UI Pattern

```
User clicks "Delete" on draft invoice →
  1. API sets deleted_at = NOW(), returns { undoToken: uuid, expiresAt: timestamp }
  2. UI shows toast: "Invoice INV-042 deleted. [Undo]" with countdown
  3. User clicks Undo → API clears deleted_at WHERE id = X AND undo_token = Y
  4. Toast expires → record stays soft-deleted, background cleanup eventually hard-deletes
```

**Scope:** Only draft/unposted entities. Posted GL entries continue to use the reversal mechanism.

#### 1.2.4 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Deleting a draft entity soft-deletes it (sets deleted_at)
- [ ] Toast notification appears with 30-second undo window
- [ ] Clicking Undo restores the entity
- [ ] Soft-deleted entities are hidden from all list views
- [ ] Posted GL entries are NOT affected (still use reversal)
- [ ] Audit log captures both delete and undo actions

## WS-2: Security & Authentication (Q2 2026) — HIGH

### Feature 2.1: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

**Gap:** JWT token auth only. No 2FA. Critical for accounting software handling sensitive financial data.

**Priority:** High
**Effort:** 2 weeks

#### 2.1.1 Database Migration — `269_two_factor_auth.sql`

```sql
-- 2FA configuration per user
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_2fa (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  method VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('totp', 'sms')),
  secret_encrypted TEXT,
  phone_number VARCHAR(20),
  is_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  is_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  backup_codes TEXT[],
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, method)
);

-- Trusted devices (skip 2FA for 30 days)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_trusted_devices (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  device_fingerprint VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  device_name VARCHAR(255),
  trusted_until TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, device_fingerprint)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_2fa_user ON user_2fa(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_trusted_devices_user ON user_trusted_devices(user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_trusted_devices_expiry ON user_trusted_devices(trusted_until);
```

#### 2.1.2 TOTP Flow

**Setup (one-time):**
1. User navigates to My Account → Security → Enable 2FA
2. Backend generates TOTP secret (using `otpauth` or `speakeasy` npm package)
3. Frontend displays QR code (otpauth:// URI) for Google Authenticator / Authy
4. User enters 6-digit code from authenticator app
5. Backend verifies code, sets `is_verified = true`, generates 10 backup codes
6. Display backup codes once (user must save them)

**Login with 2FA:**
1. User submits email + password → normal auth
2. If user has 2FA enabled → return `{ requiresTwoFactor: true, tempToken: '...' }`
3. Frontend shows 2FA code input screen
4. User enters 6-digit TOTP code (or backup code)
5. Backend verifies → issue full JWT session token
6. Optional: "Trust this device for 30 days" checkbox → creates trusted device entry

**SMS Fallback:**
1. User clicks "Use SMS instead" on 2FA screen
2. Backend sends 6-digit code via SMS (using existing emailService pattern, adapt for SMS provider)
3. Code valid for 5 minutes, single-use

#### 2.1.3 API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-setup` | Generate TOTP secret + QR code URI |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-verify-setup` | Verify initial TOTP code, enable 2FA |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-verify` | Verify TOTP/SMS code during login |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-disable` | Disable 2FA (requires current code) |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-backup-codes` | Regenerate backup codes |
| GET | `/api/auth/2fa-status` | Check if 2FA is enabled for current user |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa-sms-send` | Send SMS verification code |

#### 2.1.4 Login Flow Changes

Modify `pages/api/auth/login.ts`:
```
1. Validate email + password (existing)
2. Check user_2fa table for enabled 2FA
3. If 2FA enabled:
   a. Check trusted_devices for valid device fingerprint
   b. If trusted → skip 2FA, issue full token
   c. If not trusted → return { requiresTwoFactor: true, tempToken }
4. If 2FA not enabled → issue full token (existing flow)
```

Modify `pages/login.tsx`:
```
1. Existing login form
2. If response.requiresTwoFactor → show 2FA input screen
3. 2FA screen: 6-digit code input, "Use SMS" link, "Use backup code" link
4. "Trust this device" checkbox
5. Submit → verify → redirect to accounting
```

#### 2.1.5 Enforcement Rules

- Owner and Admin roles: 2FA strongly recommended (banner until enabled)
- All roles: 2FA optional but encouraged
- Future: company setting to enforce 2FA for all users

#### 2.1.6 UI — My Account Security Tab

Add to `pages/accounting/my-account.tsx`:
- Security section with 2FA status
- "Enable Two-Factor Authentication" button → setup wizard
- "Manage Trusted Devices" → list with remove option
- "Regenerate Backup Codes" button
- "Disable 2FA" button (requires code confirmation)

#### 2.1.7 Dependencies

- `otpauth` npm package (TOTP generation/verification)
- `qrcode` npm package (QR code generation for authenticator setup)
- SMS provider integration (Clickatell, Africa's Talking, or Twilio)

#### 2.1.8 Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] User can enable TOTP-based 2FA via QR code setup
- [ ] Login requires 2FA code when enabled
- [ ] Backup codes work as alternative to TOTP
- [ ] SMS fallback sends code and verifies correctly
- [ ] "Trust this device" skips 2FA for 30 days
- [ ] Trusted devices can be viewed and revoked
- [ ] Disabling 2FA requires current code verification
- [ ] 2FA secrets are encrypted at rest
- [ ] Audit log captures 2FA enable/disable/login events
- [ ] Rate limiting: max 5 failed 2FA attempts per 15 minutes
